headline: Googlebook launches at MacBook prices, but with major app issues
summary: Google's new Android-based laptops start at $899, yet struggle with basic apps like Slack and lack native AI tools, raising trust concerns.
details: Google has launched its new "Googlebook" laptops, running an Android-based desktop OS, with prices starting at $899. While boasting premium hardware and deep Android integration, early reviews highlight significant app compatibility issues.

Popular apps like Slack are not readily available, with the Play Store recommending a web app that fails to install properly on Googlebooks. This is despite similar workarounds existing on Chromebooks, making the issue harder to justify for a new platform.

Further complicating matters, the "Better Together" features, a key selling point for deep Android integration, require Android 17 or later and are not compatible with Samsung phones, the largest Android manufacturer.

AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude lack native desktop applications, forcing users to rely on web versions or less straightforward terminal-based solutions. This falls short of expectations for a modern laptop aiming to integrate AI workflows.
Even Apple's more affordable MacBook Neo, priced at $699, offers a more mature app ecosystem and a smoother user experience, despite its inferior hardware specifications.

The author expresses reluctance to invest in Googlebooks due to the company's history of unfinished platforms and app fragmentation, suggesting that for the same price, a MacBook provides a more reliable and functional experience.

Googlebooks aim to provide deep Android integration, but the current implementation, marred by app compatibility issues and fragmentation, fails to justify the premium price point compared to established competitors like Apple's MacBooks.

headline: Epic Games delays Disney game for "AI first" production
summary: The studio is reportedly shifting to an AI-first approach for asset generation and development, leading to a delay in its upcoming Disney title.
details: Epic Games has reportedly delayed an upcoming Disney game to adopt an "AI first" production plan, according to sources speaking with Bloomberg. This new directive aims to replace hand-written code and generate all art assets using AI workflows.

The shift to an AI-centric development model has reportedly been met with mixed reactions from employees. Epic Games has been actively integrating generative AI tools into its Unreal Engine, signaling a serious commitment to this approach.

This collaboration stems from Disney's $1.5 billion investment in Epic Games in 2024, intended to build a shared "games and entertainment universe." The delayed title was rumored to be an extraction shooter, originally slated for a November launch.
The game's release date has now been pushed back to March, even before the official AI mandate was issued. This delay is separate from the new AI-driven production strategy.

The gaming industry is seeing a growing debate around generative AI. A recent GDC survey indicated that 52% of developers view gen AI as detrimental to the industry, a significant increase from previous years.
